newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Meridor warns of further budget cuts.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Meridor warns of further budget cuts.

text.p: Israeli Finance Minister Dan Meridor said on Sunday that if it became clear that government revenues were falling at least one billion shekels short of projections, further budget cuts would be made in 1997.

Meridor's remarks came as the Treasury presented the 1997 budget to parliament. The 190.8 billion shekel budget already envisages a cut of 4.9 billion shekels in spending, with the goal of slimming Israel's deficit to 2.8 percent of gross domestic product.

Meridor did not say when the Treasury would re-examine its revenue forecast except to say that it would be soon. He noted that the Treasury had overestimated revenues in the last two years, leaving the government with a bigger-than-expected deficit.

Meridor told leaders of the Israel ba-Aliyah party, a partner in the government coalition, that he would not allocate spending for immigrant hostels without an equivalent cut somewhere else in appropriations.
Israel ba-Aliyah officials said they would only support the budget if there was special funding for the hostels as well as for integrating immigrant scientists into the workforce.
Yisrael ba-Aliyah won votes mainly from immigrants from the former Soviet Union.
Merdior noted that the funding had been a condition for the party's joining the coalition but said budget constraints limited the government's options.
